title: Script value metamethod lookup
summary: Recover VA 0x4f5d00 (106 bytes) as a read-only metatable hash-chain lookup. Tags 5 and 7 use the object's +8 metatable; other tags use global +0x7c. Event names are global +0xa0; string keys require tag 4 and interned pointer identity. Missing results return shared nil VA 0x99a41c. Original callers confirm ECX state, EDX value and caller-cleaned stack event; test-only regparm adapter preserves this custom ABI.
test_description: Direct original/recovered/expected pointer comparison for tags 0..8, events 0..17, absent object/type metatables, absent chains, direct and late matches, mismatched key tags and equal-hash distinct key pointers, nil-valued matching nodes and first-match precedence. Hashes include high bits and counts include 0, 31, 32, 33 and 255 to verify x86 shift masking. All fixture bytes are compared before/after each call; test-owned FS setup must succeed and its head must remain unchanged. Missing-table calls also test an invalid event index without accessing names. Conflicting global/object metatables establish selection precedence; an absent object metatable also permits a null global pointer. GCC harness passed; supplied VS2013 compilation passed at O1, O2 and O2 /Oy-.
known_limits: No matching-byte claim. Portable member signature models behavior rather than reproducing the original nonstandard register ABI.
Original runtime has 32-bit pointers and payloads; layouts are asserted on 32-bit builds. A 64-bit port must adapt the value payload representation and rebind the shared nil address.

Valid allocated objects, event names, bucket arrays and terminating chains are caller preconditions. Invalid pointers, out-of-range tags/events with a present metatable and cyclic chains are not made safe by this routine.
Opaque fields and semantic type names beyond observed Lua-like tags/offsets are not recovered. Large hash masks are tested with bounded bucket indices; enormous real tables are not allocated.
